Acerbic

uh-SUR-bik · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Acerbic is bitingly bitter in tone, temper, or taste; sharply critical.

The film critic's acerbic review dismissed the blockbuster as 'two hours of explosions with the emotional depth of a parking ticket.'

Worked Example

Known for his acerbic wit, the talk-show host could reduce even the most confident guest to stammering silence with a single well-aimed remark.

Acerbic describes a sharp, biting quality -- whether in someone's words, humor, or even a taste -- that stings rather than soothes.

How Acerbic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

caustic

caustic: bitterly sharp and corrosive in tone (a word you met earlier in this course)

biting

biting: sharply critical, cutting

Antonyms

gentle

gentle: mild and kind

diplomatic

diplomatic: tactful, avoiding giving offense

How Strong Is It? — blunt → vitriolic → acerbic

blunt vs. acerbic

blunt vs. acerbic: Blunt describes plainly honest speech, without necessarily being meant to wound the way acerbic can.

vitriolic vs. acerbic

vitriolic vs. acerbic: Vitriolic describes speech so venomously bitter it goes even further than acerbic's sharp bite.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — acerb-

root — acerb-: sour, harsh, bitter (Latin acerbus)

suffix — -ic

suffix — -ic: having the qualities of (Greek/Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Acerbic comes from Latin acerbus, 'sour, harsh' -- the same root behind exacerbate ('to make a bad situation more bitter, or worse'), a word from earlier in this course. Someone acerbic has a sour, biting sharpness to their words.

Use the root in a new word: exacerbate

Use the root in a new word: exacerbate: Yelling at the crying toddler only served to exacerbate the tantrum, not calm it.

Word Choice

Acerbic praises precision, not cruelty -- it's the word for wit or criticism so sharp it almost has a taste, biting and memorable rather than simply mean.
